body:
The diagram below shows the process of making compost from garden waste and food scraps.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: How compost is made from garden and food waste
steps: Garden waste and food scraps are collected separately from household rubbish
Woody branches are shredded into small pieces
Shredded wood is mixed with food scraps and grass clippings
The mixture is piled into long rows called windrows
The windrows are turned regularly so that air reaches the centre
Heat from microbial activity raises the temperature of the pile to about 60°C
Liquid draining from the pile is collected and sprayed back over the rows
The material is screened to remove large pieces that have not decomposed
Oversized pieces are returned to the start of the process
The screened material is left to mature for about three months
Samples are tested for moisture, nutrients and contaminants
Finished compost is bagged or sold in bulk to farms and gardeners

body:
The plans below show a disused railway yard as it is now and the arts quarter planned for 2030.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

chart.title: A railway yard before and after its conversion into an arts quarter

before.label: Now
features: Engine shed with a long curved roof in the north-west corner
Goods warehouse along the eastern boundary, next to the canal
Four sets of railway tracks running east to west across the centre
Signal box beside the main gate on the southern edge
Water tower opposite the engine shed
Coal store at the south end of the yard
Footbridge linking the yard to the housing estate in the north
Office block next to the signal box
Wasteland of weeds between the tracks and the canal
Access road from the main gate to the goods warehouse

after.label: 2030 (planned)
features: Engine shed converted into a theatre, keeping its roof
Goods warehouse turned into artist studios, next to the canal
Tracks removed from the centre and replaced by a public square
Signal box kept as a café beside the main gate
Water tower repainted and fitted with a climbing wall, opposite the theatre
Coal store demolished to make room for a sculpture park at the south end
Footbridge widened and now linking the square to the housing estate in the north
New gallery built on the site of the office block, next to the signal box
Gardens and wetland between the square and the canal
Bus stop moved from the main gate to the edge of the square
